new_supplier_proposal.complete_short_proof_plan:
Choose one ordered orthonormal basis e_1,...,e_D and identify B(H) with M_D(C), using the root linear-first convention <x,y>=sum x_i conjugate(y_i), so rank-one |v><v| sends x to <x,v>v and has matrix vv*. Matrix composition and conjugate-transpose obey associative/bilinear algebra and involution rules. The induced operator norm is a norm (apply each operator to unit vectors), is submultiplicative and satisfies ||A*A||=||A||^2 by the exact published operator-norm corollary. Its C*-identity applied to A and A* plus submultiplicativity gives ||A*||=||A||, treating A=0 separately. Matrix units form a finite ordered basis of the normed matrix space, so the exact published finite-dimensional Banach corollary proves completeness. Since D>=1, I is nonzero and ||I||=1. These verify the actual canonical def-c-star-algebra, not only a named C*-identity.
For any complex-linear functional omega positive in the canonical sense omega(B*B)>=0, set rho_ij=omega(E_ji). Finite expansion A=sum_ij A_ij E_ij gives omega(A)=Tr(rho A) for every complex matrix A. For any z in C^D, take B=e_1 z*, so B*B=zz*. Hence z* rho z=omega(zz*)>=0 is real. The tests z=e_i, e_i+e_j and e_i+i e_j show rho_ii real and rho_ij=conjugate(rho_ji); thus rho is Hermitian, and the already obtained quadratic inequality makes it positive. Also Tr rho=sum_i omega(E_ii)=omega(I). Conversely, for any rho>=0, diagonalize it with the preserved spectral supplier as rho=sum p_j u_j u_j*, p_j>=0. For EVERY complex A, omega_rho(A)=sum_j p_j <Au_j,u_j>, so |omega_rho(A)|<=sum_j p_j ||A|| by vector Cauchy-Schwarz. Thus omega_rho is bounded with norm at most Tr rho, and its value at I (whose norm is one) proves norm exactly Tr rho. Positivity holds since omega_rho(B*B)=sum_j p_j ||B u_j||^2>=0. Uniqueness follows by evaluating at all E_ji. Therefore canonical states (positive functional with norm one) are exactly canonical QC densities (positive endomorphism with trace one), and for positive finite functionals norm one is equivalent to omega(I)=1. The zero functional corresponds to rho=0 and norm zero, so no normalization division by zero is hidden. Repeated eigenvalues and nonfaithful densities are allowed. The dimension restriction excludes H=0, while an empty spin region has H=C, D=1 and is included. Finally ||A||^2 I-A*A is positive by its quadratic form and has a positive square root from the original spectral supplier, supplying the local order estimate needed by GNS. All matrix formulas are finite; no arbitrary family or countable selection is made.
